introduction.title: Introduction
introduction.description: What BFlow is and how your money is organized in the app.

sections.title: What is BFlow?
body: BFlow is a personal and shared finance tool. It brings your income, expenses, budgets and wallets together so you always know how much you have, where it goes and how much is left.
You can use it on your own or invite your partner, family or friends to manage a wallet together.

sections.title: How it is organized
body: Everything in BFlow revolves around four connected pieces:
items: Wallets: each account, card or cash balance you want to track.
Transactions: the income, expenses and transfers you record in a wallet.
Budgets: spending limits per wallet, per category or both.
Members: the people you share a wallet with.

sections.title: Currency
body: For now, every wallet, transaction and budget is handled in US dollars (USD).
sections.note: The currency is assigned automatically when you create a wallet and cannot be changed.

plans.title: Plans and limits
plans.description: What each plan includes and how payments are processed.

sections.title: Personal
body: The free plan, designed to start organizing your finances at no cost.
items: Up to 2 wallets.
Up to 2 recurring transactions.
Up to 3 budgets.
Join one shared wallet with up to 3 people.

sections.title: BFlow Pro
body: For people who manage several accounts or share their finances. It costs $9.99 per month or $99.99 per year.
items: Up to 100 wallets.
Up to 25 recurring transactions.
Up to 100 budgets.
Create shared wallets and invite up to 10 people.
Transfers between wallets.

sections.title: Payments
body: Plan payments are processed through Wompi. All prices are in USD; the final amount in local currency depends on your bank's exchange rate.
sections.note: You can review or cancel your subscription from Settings, in the Subscription section.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.description: Your financial summary: balance, statistics, budgets and recent activity.

sections.title: Overview
body: The dashboard is the first screen after you sign in. It greets you based on the time of day and shows how your money is doing right now.

sections.title: What it shows
body: The screen is split into cards, each with part of your information:
items: Total balance, average income and average expense, compared with last month.
Statistics: a chart of income and expenses per month. Click a legend item to show only that series.
Budget health: the status of each active budget.
This month: how your activity splits between income, expenses and transfers.
Recent activity: your latest transactions.

sections.title: Budget health
body: Each budget shows a label based on how much of its limit you have spent:
items: Healthy: you are below the alert threshold.
Warning: you passed the alert threshold.
Critical: you passed the critical threshold.
Exceeded: you spent 100% or more of the limit.

sections.title: Quick actions
body: From the dashboard you can record a new transaction or schedule a recurring one without opening a wallet. Just pick the wallet in the form.
sections.note: From here you can only record income and expenses in your own wallets. Transfers are made from a wallet's detail page.

wallets.title: Wallets
wallets.description: Create a wallet for each account, card or cash balance and check its balance and transactions.

sections.title: Create a wallet
body: In Wallets, click Create wallet and fill in the form:
items: Wallet name.
Description, for example "Savings account" or "Everyday expenses".
Initial balance: the amount you start with. It must be 0 or more.
sections.note: All wallets are created in USD.

sections.title: Your wallets
body: The list has two tabs: My wallets, with the ones you created, and Shared, with other people's wallets you joined. You can search by name and choose how many appear per page.
On the right you will see the history with your latest transactions across all wallets.

sections.title: Wallet detail
body: When you open a wallet you will see its current balance and these tabs:
items: All transactions, Income and Expenses, with search and pagination.
Transfers, only in wallets with a single member.
Members, to see and manage who has access.
Settings, with the wallet's details and options.

sections.title: Information panel
body: The side panel summarizes the last activity, the highest expense, the number of transactions and the initial value. It also lists upcoming scheduled transactions. You can hide it with Hide info.

sections.title: Edit or delete
body: In the Settings tab, the owner can change the name and description. Other members can see these details but cannot edit them.
sections.note: Deleting a wallet removes its history, budgets and members. This action cannot be undone.

sharedWallets.title: Shared wallets
sharedWallets.description: Manage a wallet as a team: invite people, assign roles and know who recorded each transaction.

sections.title: How they work
body: A wallet becomes shared when you invite someone else. Every member sees the same balance and transactions, and each transaction shows who recorded it.

sections.title: Roles
body: Each member has a role in the wallet:
items: Owner: the person who created the wallet. They can invite and remove members, edit the details and delete it.
Member: takes part by recording and viewing transactions.
Read only: can view the wallet's information.

sections.title: Invite people
body: From the Members tab, the owner clicks Invite and searches for the person by name or email (at least 2 characters). The invitation is sent by email. Each result shows whether the person can be invited:
items: Available: the person can be invited.
Already a member: they already have access to the wallet.
Invitation pending: they already have an unanswered invitation.

sections.title: Respond to an invitation
body: Your invitations appear in Wallets, under the Invitations button. Each one shows who invited you, the wallet and its expiration date. You can choose Join or Decline.
Expired invitations can no longer be accepted. The owner can cancel pending invitations from Sent invitations.

sections.title: Manage members
body: The owner can remove any member from the Members tab, and that person loses access immediately. The owner cannot remove themselves.
sections.note: Transfers are not available in shared wallets. They can only be made in wallets with a single member.

transactions.title: Transactions
transactions.description: Record income, expenses and transfers, and choose which ones repeat.

sections.title: Transaction types
body: When you click New transaction you choose one of these types:
items: Income: money coming into the wallet.
Expense: money leaving the wallet.
Transfer: money moving from one of your wallets to another.

sections.title: Income and expense details
body: Both forms ask for the same information:
items: Title.
Description, required for expenses and optional for income.
Amount, greater than 0.
Date, today by default.
Category, filtered by type.

sections.title: Recurring income and expenses
body: Turn on Recurring income or Recurring expense and choose a pattern: daily, weekly, monthly or yearly. If you need start and end dates, use Schedule transaction.

sections.title: Transfers
body: Choose the destination wallet (or the source, using the button that reverses the direction), the amount and the reason for the transfer. You can only transfer between your own wallets.
sections.note: Transfers are only available in wallets with a single member.

sections.title: Edit, delete and duplicate
body: From each transaction's menu you can update or delete income and expenses. Transfers cannot be edited or deleted.
Duplicate creates a copy dated today, useful for expenses that repeat without a fixed frequency.

scheduledTransactions.title: Scheduled transactions
scheduledTransactions.description: Let fixed payments and income record themselves.

sections.title: When to use them
body: Schedule a transaction for payments or income that repeat, such as rent, a subscription or your salary. BFlow records them automatically on each date.

sections.title: Schedule a transaction
body: Click Schedule transaction from the dashboard or from a wallet's information panel, and fill in:
items: Type: income or expense.
Title, description, amount and category.
Frequency: daily, weekly, monthly or yearly.
Every: how many days, weeks, months or years between repetitions.
Start date and end date.
sections.note: The end date is required and must be the same as or later than the start date.

sections.title: Upcoming transactions
body: In each wallet's detail page, the Upcoming section lists the scheduled transactions about to be recorded.

history.title: History
history.description: All your transactions grouped by day, across every wallet.

sections.title: Overview
body: History brings together the transactions from all your wallets, grouped by day. You can reach it from Wallets › History or with See more in the history panel.

sections.title: Filters
body: Search by text or filter by type: All, Income, Expenses or Transfers.

sections.title: What each transaction shows
body: Each card shows the title, wallet, category, amount and whether it was recorded manually or as a recurrence. Transfers also show the counterpart wallet.
sections.note: From history you can view the details or duplicate a transaction. To edit or delete it, open it from its wallet.

budgets.title: Budgets
budgets.description: Set a limit on your spending and get alerts before you go over.

sections.title: Scope
body: A budget can track different groups of expenses:
items: Wallet: every expense in a wallet.
Category: the expenses in a category across all your wallets.
Wallet + category: the expenses in a category within a wallet.

sections.title: Create a budget
body: In Budgets, click Create budget, choose the scope and fill in the amount, the period (daily, weekly, monthly or yearly) and the start date.

sections.title: Thresholds and statuses
body: Each budget has two thresholds that define its status. By default, the alert is at 60% and the critical threshold at 90%; the critical threshold must always be higher than the alert.
items: Healthy: below the alert.
Warning: from the alert threshold.
Critical: from the critical threshold.
Exceeded: from 100% of the limit.

sections.title: Tracking
body: A budget's detail page shows how much is left and how many days remain, the amount spent with its daily average, a progress bar with the thresholds and the spending trend.

sections.title: Edit or delete
body: In the Settings tab you can change the amount, period, start date and thresholds, or delete the budget.
sections.note: The wallet and category cannot be changed after the budget is created.

categories.title: Categories
categories.description: Classify your income and expenses to understand where your money goes.

sections.title: What they are for
body: Every income and expense has a category. Categories let you create category budgets and better understand your transactions.

sections.title: Create a category
body: Go to Settings › Categories › Manage and fill in:
items: Name.
Type: expense or income.
Color and icon, to recognize it quickly.
sections.note: Categories cannot be edited or deleted for now.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.description: Stay up to date with what happens in your wallets and budgets.

sections.title: Where to find them
body: Click the bell at the top of the app. The number shows how many unread notifications you have.

sections.title: Mark as read
body: Each notification has a Mark as read option. When none are left, you will see the message You are all caught up.

settings.title: Settings
settings.description: Manage your profile, language, subscription and session.

sections.title: Profile
body: Click the pencil next to your name to change your name or photo (PNG, JPEG or WebP). Your email cannot be changed.

sections.title: Language
body: Choose between Spanish and English. Your preference is saved to your profile.

sections.title: Subscription
body: If you have a paid plan, you will see the current plan, its status, the price, the next billing date and how long it is valid. You can also cancel it from here.

sections.title: Sign out
body: At the bottom of Settings you will find the button to sign out.

claude.title: Claude connection
claude.description: Ask about your financial information in natural language from Claude.

sections.title: What it is
body: BFlow can be added to Claude as a custom connector. That way you can ask questions about your finances without opening the app.

sections.title: How to connect it
body: Connecting takes a few steps:
items: Go to Settings and click Connect with Claude.
Claude will open with the BFlow connector already set up.
Confirm the connection in Claude.

sections.title: What you can ask
body: Some examples:
items: How much did I spend on food this month?
How are my budgets doing?
What is the balance of my savings wallet?

faq.question: Why use BFlow?
faq.answer: BFlow brings your income, expenses, budgets and wallets together so you can understand your money every day.

faq.question: Can I share my wallets?
faq.answer: Yes. You can create shared wallets and invite the people you manage your finances with.

faq.question: Which payment gateway does BFlow use?
faq.answer: Premium plan payments are processed through Wompi, an online payment platform.

faq.question: Is my data safe?

faq.question: Can I change or cancel my plan?
